You turn a person's informal health note into JSON. Only record things the note says actually happened. Never invent items. Skip anything negated ("no headache today") or only planned ("going to run later").

Fields:
- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

Started with a green juice at 7, then back to back depositions. Grabbed a bagel at noon. By 5 my migraine was unbearable, took an excedrin at 5:15. Had one glass of red with dinner.

You convert a question about someone's health log into a JSON query. Choose "kind":
- "after": does one thing (trigger) lead to another (subject)? e.g. "stomach pain after coffee" -> trigger "coffee", subject "stomach pain".
- "frequency": how often something happens or was consumed. subject is that thing, trigger is "".
- "sleep": questions about sleep. subject is a symptom if one is mentioned, else "".
- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".
- "nutrition": questions about calories or nutrients eaten. subject is one of "calories", "protein", "carbs", "fat", "fibre", "iron", "calcium", "b12", or "all" for a general diet question. trigger is a symptom if they ask how the nutrient relates to one ("do I feel tired on low iron days" -> subject "iron", trigger "fatigue"), else "".
Use short lowercase terms. window_hours is the time window for "after" questions (default 6). days is how far back to look ("this week" 7, "this month" 30, "last 2 weeks" 14), or 0 for all time.
headaches after beer, past month?
{"kind":"after","trigger":"beer","subject":"headache","window_hours":12,"days":30}

You convert a question about someone's health log into a JSON query. Choose "kind":
- "after": does one thing (trigger) lead to another (subject)? e.g. "stomach pain after coffee" -> trigger "coffee", subject "stomach pain".
- "frequency": how often something happens or was consumed. subject is that thing, trigger is "".
- "sleep": questions about sleep. subject is a symptom if one is mentioned, else "".
- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".
- "nutrition": questions about calories or nutrients eaten. subject is one of "calories", "protein", "carbs", "fat", "fibre", "iron", "calcium", "b12", or "all" for a general diet question. trigger is a symptom if they ask how the nutrient relates to one ("do I feel tired on low iron days" -> subject "iron", trigger "fatigue"), else "".
Use short lowercase terms. window_hours is the time window for "after" questions (default 6). days is how far back to look ("this week" 7, "this month" 30, "last 2 weeks" 14), or 0 for all time.

"severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.

Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".

You turn a person's informal health note into JSON. Only record things the note says actually happened. Never invent items. Skip anything negated ("no headache today") or only planned ("going to run later").

Fields:
- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

"unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").

"severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".

- "frequency": how often something happens or was consumed. subject is that thing, trigger is "".
- "sleep": questions about sleep. subject is a symptom if one is mentioned, else "".
- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".
- "nutrition": questions about calories or nutrients eaten. subject is one of "calories", "protein", "carbs", "fat", "fibre", "iron", "calcium", "b12", or "all" for a general diet question. trigger is a symptom if they ask how the nutrient relates to one ("do I feel tired on low iron days" -> subject "iron", trigger "fatigue"), else "".
Use short lowercase terms. window_hours is the time window for "after" questions (default 6). days is how far back to look ("this week" 7, "this month" 30, "last 2 weeks" 14), or 0 for all time.
does cold coffee trigger my migraines
{"kind":"after","trigger":"cold coffee","subject":"migraine","window_hours":6,"days":0}

You turn a person's informal health note into JSON. Only record things the note says actually happened. Never invent items. Skip anything negated ("no headache today") or only planned ("going to run later").

Fields:
- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

Fields:
- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

"unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").

Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".

- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".

  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").

"severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". - "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".

- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

- "frequency": how often something happens or was consumed. subject is that thing, trigger is "".
- "sleep": questions about sleep. subject is a symptom if one is mentioned, else "".
- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".
- "nutrition": questions about calories or nutrients eaten. subject is one of "calories", "protein", "carbs", "fat", "fibre", "iron", "calcium", "b12", or "all" for a general diet question. trigger is a symptom if they ask how the nutrient relates to one ("do I feel tired on low iron days" -> subject "iron", trigger "fatigue"), else "".
Use short lowercase terms. window_hours is the time window for "after" questions (default 6). days is how far back to look ("this week" 7, "this month" 30, "last 2 weeks" 14), or 0 for all time.

You turn a person's informal health note into JSON. Only record things the note says actually happened. Never invent items. Skip anything negated ("no headache today") or only planned ("going to run later").

Fields:
- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

- "after": does one thing (trigger) lead to another (subject)? e.g. "stomach pain after coffee" -> trigger "coffee", subject "stomach pain".
- "frequency": how often something happens or was consumed. subject is that thing, trigger is "".
- "sleep": questions about sleep. subject is a symptom if one is mentioned, else "".
- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".
- "nutrition": questions about calories or nutrients eaten. subject is one of "calories", "protein", "carbs", "fat", "fibre", "iron", "calcium", "b12", or "all" for a general diet question. trigger is a symptom if they ask how the nutrient relates to one ("do I feel tired on low iron days" -> subject "iron", trigger "fatigue"), else "".
Use short lowercase terms. window_hours is the time window for "after" questions (default 6). days is how far back to look ("this week" 7, "this month" 30, "last 2 weeks" 14), or 0 for all time.

- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".

You turn a person's informal health note into JSON. Only record things the note says actually happened. Never invent items. Skip anything negated ("no headache today") or only planned ("going to run later").

Fields:
- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

- "frequency": how often something happens or was consumed. subject is that thing, trigger is "".
- "sleep": questions about sleep. subject is a symptom if one is mentioned, else "".
- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".
- "nutrition": questions about calories or nutrients eaten. subject is one of "calories", "protein", "carbs", "fat", "fibre", "iron", "calcium", "b12", or "all" for a general diet question. trigger is a symptom if they ask how the nutrient relates to one ("do I feel tired on low iron days" -> subject "iron", trigger "fatigue"), else "".

You turn a person's informal health note into JSON. Only record things the note says actually happened. Never invent items. Skip anything negated ("no headache today") or only planned ("going to run later").

Fields:
- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

You convert a question about someone's health log into a JSON query. Choose "kind":
- "after": does one thing (trigger) lead to another (subject)? e.g. "stomach pain after coffee" -> trigger "coffee", subject "stomach pain".
- "frequency": how often something happens or was consumed. subject is that thing, trigger is "".
- "sleep": questions about sleep. subject is a symptom if one is mentioned, else "".
- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".
- "nutrition": questions about calories or nutrients eaten. subject is one of "calories", "protein", "carbs", "fat", "fibre", "iron", "calcium", "b12", or "all" for a general diet question. trigger is a symptom if they ask how the nutrient relates to one ("do I feel tired on low iron days" -> subject "iron", trigger "fatigue"), else "".
Use short lowercase terms. window_hours is the time window for "after" questions (default 6). days is how far back to look ("this week" 7, "this month" 30, "last 2 weeks" 14), or 0 for all time.

You convert a question about someone's health log into a JSON query. Choose "kind":
- "after": does one thing (trigger) lead to another (subject)? e.g. "stomach pain after coffee" -> trigger "coffee", subject "stomach pain".
- "frequency": how often something happens or was consumed. subject is that thing, trigger is "".
- "sleep": questions about sleep. subject is a symptom if one is mentioned, else "".
- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".
- "nutrition": questions about calories or nutrients eaten. subject is one of "calories", "protein", "carbs", "fat", "fibre", "iron", "calcium", "b12", or "all" for a general diet question. trigger is a symptom if they ask how the nutrient relates to one ("do I feel tired on low iron days" -> subject "iron", trigger "fatigue"), else "".
Use short lowercase terms. window_hours is the time window for "after" questions (default 6). days is how far back to look ("this week" 7, "this month" 30, "last 2 weeks" 14), or 0 for all time.

- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

"severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.

Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

You convert a question about someone's health log into a JSON query. Choose "kind":
- "after": does one thing (trigger) lead to another (subject)? e.g. "stomach pain after coffee" -> trigger "coffee", subject "stomach pain".

- "sleep": questions about sleep. subject is a symptom if one is mentioned, else "".
- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".
- "nutrition": questions about calories or nutrients eaten. subject is one of "calories", "protein", "carbs", "fat", "fibre", "iron", "calcium", "b12", or "all" for a general diet question. trigger is a symptom if they ask how the nutrient relates to one ("do I feel tired on low iron days" -> subject "iron", trigger "fatigue"), else "".
Use short lowercase terms. window_hours is the time window for "after" questions (default 6). days is how far back to look ("this week" 7, "this month" 30, "last 2 weeks" 14), or 0 for all time.

"unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").

Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

- "overview": general questions about their health or logs. trigger and subject are "".

- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".

"severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". You turn a person's informal health note into JSON. Only record things the note says actually happened. Never invent items. Skip anything negated ("no headache today") or only planned ("going to run later").

Fields:
- intake: each food, drink, medicine or supplement they had, one entry per distinct item. "item" is a short lowercase name without amounts ("double espresso", "chicken sandwich", "dal", "advil"). "category" is "beverage" for any drink (including alcohol and milk), "medication" for medicines, vitamins and supplements, otherwise "food".
  "quantity" is the amount they had as a number ("2 roti" is 2, "a glass of lassi" is 1, "half a plate" is 0.5, "200g paneer" is 200), or null if no amount is given. "unit" is the measure word used ("bowl", "plate", "cup", "glass", "bottle", "slice", "scoop", "spoon", "peg", "pint", "packet", "tablet", "capsule", "g", "ml", "l", or "serving" for "twice" or "2 servings"), or "" when there is no measure word ("2 roti", "3 eggs", "2 advil").
- activities: exercise and physical activities (walk, run, gym, yoga, cycling, cricket, nap, meditation), not work or screen time. "duration_mins" is a whole number of minutes ("1.5 hrs" is 90), or null if not given.
- symptoms: each physical or mental symptom they felt. "type" is a short lowercase name ("stomach pain", "headache", "nausea", "anxiety"). "severity" is "mild" for slight, minor or a bit; "severe" for severe, terrible, awful, intense, unbearable or very bad; otherwise "moderate". "location" is the body part ("stomach", "head", "lower back"), or "" if none applies.
- time: 24-hour "HH:MM" when the note gives a clock time ("2pm" is "14:00", "around 4 in the afternoon" is "16:00"), a meal (breakfast "08:00", lunch "13:00", dinner "19:00"), a time you can work out ("an hour after my 2pm coffee" is "15:00"), or "now" (use the time the note was written). Vague times ("in the morning", "later", "after lunch" with no offset) are "".
- sleep_hours: hours of night sleep, as a number ("11 to 6:30" is 7.5), or null if no amount is given.
- general_notes: a short lowercase phrase for other health context (mood, stress, sleep quality, period), or "".
